subject: EdgeMetric POC - observability checklist, success criteria & timeline
messages:
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sara Patel <sara@edgemetric.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynold@edgemetric.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeMetric POC - observability checklist, success criteria & timeline

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed observability plan for the POC so your engineering team can evaluate readiness and success metrics. I captured owners and a suggested 3-week timeline below.

1) Objective (POC scope)
- Validate Redwood Inference with EdgeMetric's sample workloads: inference latency (real-time scoring), throughput for batch scoring, and cost/per-token estimates on a representative dataset.

2) Success criteria (agreed pass/fail checkpoints)
- Latency: p50 < 80 ms, p95 < 200 ms for live scoring in our test region.
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s with average tokens/request ~150 during batch windows.
- Cost: estimated per-1M token cost <= your internal threshold (we'll provide breakdown).
- Functional: tracing shows end-to-end request path across client -> Redwood API -> model shard; no more than 1% error rate (5xx and parse errors).
- Observability: dashboards and alerts in place (see below) and log export to your S3 bucket

3) Observability deliverables (what Redwood will set up during POC)
- Dashboards (Grafana/Redwood Console):
  * Inference latency: p50/p90/p95, broken down by model/version and route.
  * Token throughput: tokens/sec, tokens/request histogram.
  * Inference errors: 4xx/5xx rate, parse failures, rate-limited requests.
  * Model-level metrics: KV cache hit rate, cache size, GPU utilization, memory pressure.
  * Cost telemetry: estimated per-token cost and projected monthly spend at measured throughput.
- Tracing: Distributed traces with request IDs surfaced in Redwood Console and a Jaeger-compatible export. Sample trace will include client span, Redwood ingress, model runtime span, and response serialization span.
- Logs: Structured request/response logging (redacted PII) exported to s3://edgemetric-poc-logs/ with daily rollover.
- Alerts & SLOs: Pager alert for p95 latency breach (>200ms for 5m) and error-rate >1% for 10m. Slack webhook to your #ai-ops channel.

4) Ownership & contacts
- Redwood: Kimberly Park (POC lead) — kimberly_park@redwood.ai (overall coordination); Marcus Lin (observability engineer) — marcus_lin@redwood.ai (dashboards/tracing); Jordan Blake (solutions) — jordan_blake@redwood.ai (integration & prompts).
- EdgeMetric: Sara Patel (data platform) and Tom Reynolds (ML infra).

5) Timeline (recommended)
- Week 0 (by Apr 16): SOW & onboarding; credentials + S3 bucket + sample workload ingestion.
- Week 1 (Apr 19–23): Baseline runs, initial dashboards, tracing enabled.
- Week 2 (Apr 26–30): Load testing, alert fine-tuning, cost estimates.
- Week 3 (May 3–7): Final validation, findings, and next-step recommendation.

6) Action items / next steps (what we need from EdgeMetric)
- Provide short-term access: API key or temporary VPC route; S3 write permissions for log export.
- Confirm target success thresholds (especially cost threshold).
- Procurement contact for SOW: please loop in someone we can send a one-page SOW to (PDF attached).

Attachments: edgemetric-poc-observability-checklist.xlsx (proposed dashboard/metric list), redwood-poc-sow-v1.pdf (one-page SOW)

Would you be able to confirm the S3 bucket name and preferred Slack channel by end of day Thursday? Once we have that I'll get Marcus to provision the dashboards and start tracing.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@edgemetric.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@edgemetric.com>, procure@edgemetric.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeMetric POC - observability checklist, success criteria & timeline

Kimberly —

Thanks for the thorough summary. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications:
- SLOs look reasonable; we'll confirm the cost threshold internally (aiming for <= $12 / 1M tokens for the POC).
- For tracing we prefer traces include a correlation_id set by our gateway; can Redwood ingest and echo that header?
- We'll provide an S3 bucket (edgemetric-poc-logs) and will add redwood-poc@edgemetric.com as a writer.

Procurement (cc'd) — please confirm who should receive the SOW and whether a short MSFT purchase order is required for POC access.

I'll confirm the Slack channel tomorrow.

Appreciate it —
Tom

On Tue, Apr 13, 2027 at 09:30 AM kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Tom — great, thanks. Yes we can ingest a correlation_id header and surface it in the trace.
> I'll add that to the tracing checklist.
>
> Marcus — can you scope the dashboard that surfaces correlation_id in trace links and make sure Jaeger export includes it?
>
> Procurement: we typically send a short SOW and invoice for a one-month trial; is that OK? If PO is needed we can route through the invoice flow.
>
> Kimberly

---

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeMetric POC - observability checklist, success criteria & timeline

Kimberly / Jordan / Laura —

I'll take point on dashboard and tracing setup. Plan below:

- Day 1 (Apr 19): Deploy baseline Redwood Console dashboard with latency, errors, tokens/sec. Configure trace ingestion and map correlation_id to trace tags.
- Day 2 (Apr 20): Add model-level panels (KV cache hit rate, GPU util). Hook Jaeger export and test with correlation IDs.
- Day 3 (Apr 21): Wire S3 export for structured logs and validate redaction rules.
- Alerts: implement p95 latency and error rate alerts; add Slack webhook placeholder for EdgeMetric channel.

I estimate 4–6 hours of coordination with EdgeMetric engineers during Day 1 & 2 to confirm mapping and sample traces.

I'll attach the dashboard JSON and a short runbook after Day 1.

Marcus Lin
Observability Engineer, Redwood Inference
